passage: Friday: Hemant and Omkar fought over the last mango slice, and Omkar called his big brother Hemant stupid. A cushion flew across the room. Saturday: They argued about the remote, about whose shoe was on whose side, and Hemant shouted, "You are the worst brother ever!" Omkar cried a little and stormed out. Sunday: The power went off in the rain. They dragged bedsheets and chairs into the middle of the room and built a fort by torchlight. "Sorry I said worst," Hemant muttered. "Sorry I said stupid," said Omkar. They lay inside whispering jokes until Mummy peeked in, smiled and switched off the fan.

qa.q: What did the brothers build on Sunday night?
qa.a: They built a fort out of bedsheets and chairs.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling when he muttered his apology in the fort?
qa.a: He probably felt regret about the hurtful thing he said and wanted to make up, since he apologised first. 🙂

qa.q: What helped the brothers repair after two days of fighting?
qa.a: They apologised for the specific insults and then did something fun together, building the fort.

qa.q: How might Omkar have felt when Hemant called him the worst brother ever?
qa.a: Omkar cried a little and stormed out, so the insult hurt him even though the brothers made up later.

grounding: Two siblings fight for days and then build a fort together, mixing irritation and love.

passage:
All Saturday, Wei and her little brother Alejandro fought. Over the TV remote. Over the last dumpling. Over whose turn it was to feed the cat. At lunch Alejandro called her "bossy cow," and Wei called him "baby." Both of them went quiet after that.
By evening, it was pouring outside. Alejandro dragged the couch cushions into a heap. "Want to build a fort?"
Wei hesitated. Then she grabbed a sheet. "Only if I'm the captain."
They made a fort with a flashlight inside. Alejandro whispered, "Sorry I called you a cow."
Wei nudged him. "Sorry I called you a baby. You're a good fort builder."

qa.q: What did Alejandro call Wei at lunch?
What mix of feelings did Wei have when Alejandro suggested building a fort?
qa.a: She still felt a bit hurt and irritated from the fighting, but also fond of him and wanted to play.

qa.q: What did the siblings do that helped mend the day?
qa.a: They apologised quickly for the insults and remembered the fun of building the fort together.

qa.q: How might Alejandro feel when Wei says he's a good fort builder?
qa.a: Alejandro likely feels happy and forgiven, glad they are friends again.

grounding: A brother and sister fight all day, trade insults, then build a fort together and apologise, showing siblings mix love and irritation.

passage:
After school, Sangeeta and her brother Arnab went to the crèche at their mother's office. They fought the whole afternoon: about crayons, about who got the swing, about the wrong answer in a puzzle. Arnab said, "You're so stupid," and Sangeeta cried in the corner.
When the crèche emptied out, they found a stack of old cardboard boxes. Sangeeta pushed one towards Arnab without saying anything. He pushed one back. Slowly they built a castle with windows.
"Sorry I said you're stupid," Arnab mumbled.
"You were a bit annoying," said Sangeeta, "but this castle is the best."
When their mother came, they were both inside it, laughing.

qa.q: Where did Sangeeta and Arnab go after school?
qa.a: To the crèche at their mother's office.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta feel when Arnab called her stupid?
qa.a: She felt hurt, crying in the corner.
Building a castle together from boxes and Arnab saying sorry quickly.

qa.q: How might their mother feel finding them laughing inside the castle?
qa.a: Their mother would likely feel relieved and pleased to see them getting along.

grounding: A sister and brother fight all afternoon, then build a cardboard castle together and apologise, showing love and irritation mixed.
